batch: Abraham scenes indices 15–24 derived from source scenes array

scenes.title: The birth of Ishmael
scenes.personsExplicitOrCollective: Hagar; Angel of the Lord; Abram; Sarai; Ishmael (named prenatally)
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: The narrative explicitly places Hagar's flight by a spring on the way to Shur (16:7); after return, Ishmael is born. This is a sequence of wilderness encounter and household birth, not one fixed Mamre scene. The Angel of the Lord, Hagar, Abram and Sarai are named; Ishmael is named by the angel before birth.

geography.claim: Shur road/spring is textual but unidentified; household birth location not stated. Split route and birth; no Mamre point.
sources: Abram's son by Hagar, explicitly named Ishmael; distinct from the Isaac line (Gen 16:11–16; compare Gen 17:18–21). No covenant rite occurs.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Abram's son by Hagar, explicitly named Ishmael; distinct from the Isaac line (Gen 16:11–16; compare Gen 17:18–21). No covenant rite occurs.

scenes.title: Abraham receives a new name
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Genesis 17:1–14 opens with the LORD appearing to Abram and renaming him Abraham; Sarai becomes Sarah in vv15–16, outside current selection. The selected unit includes covenant sign and household obligations, so the scene title should not imply only renaming.

geography.claim: No place named in 17:1–14. Mamre appears in 18:1, not here; classify unlocated.
sources: Explicit covenant with Abraham and descendants (17:2–8), circumcision sign (17:9–14); Ishmael is included in household sign while covenant line is promised through Isaac in 17:19–21. Genealogy distinctions must remain.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Explicit covenant with Abraham and descendants (17:2–8), circumcision sign (17:9–14); Ishmael is included in household sign while covenant line is promised through Isaac in 17:19–21. Genealogy distinctions must remain.

scenes.title: Three visitors at Mamre
scenes.personsExplicitOrCollective: LORD (narrative framing), Abraham, Sarah, three visitors/men; servants/bread preparation in collective terms
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Genesis 18:1–15 identifies the scene as the oaks of Mamre; three men/visitors arrive, Abraham hosts, Sarah listens and laughs, and the birth promise is spoken. Registry overlaps Atlas only for 18:1–8, omitting the promise dialogue 9–15; preserve overlap classification rather than equating full scenes.

geography.claim: Oaks of Mamre are text-exact region; exact trees/encampment unknown. Do not assert visitors' identities beyond textual/narrative identification.
sources: Promise of Sarah's son Isaac, covenant/genealogy sequence; explicit Sarah/Abraham parental promise, distinct from Ishmael.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Promise of Sarah's son Isaac, covenant/genealogy sequence; explicit Sarah/Abraham parental promise, distinct from Ishmael.

scenes.title: Abraham intercedes for Sodom
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Genesis 18:16–33 continues directly from the visitors' departure and Abraham's escort; the LORD's announcement and Abraham's intercession concern Sodom. Scene requires Mamre context for continuity, but no new physical site inside Mamre is pinpointed.

geography.claim: Mamre region as narrative context; no exact location for dialogue. Sodom itself is destination/topic, not scene location.
sources: No genealogy event; Abraham is covenant recipient and intercedes for others (Gen 18:18–19).

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: No genealogy event; Abraham is covenant recipient and intercedes for others (Gen 18:18–19).

scenes.title: The destruction of Sodom
scenes.personsExplicitOrCollective: Two angels; Lot; Lot's household; men of Sodom; LORD; Abraham referenced in v29
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Genesis 19:1–29 narrates the two angels' arrival at Sodom, Lot's hospitality, departure and destruction; v29 links the rescue to God's remembrance of Abraham. The 'Dead Sea basin' is a regional inference from later biblical geography, not a coordinate in this passage.

geography.claim: Sodom is exact textual city name, but archaeological site UNKNOWN/DISPUTED; 'Dead Sea basin' is a regional proposal only.
sources: Lot is Abraham's kinsman; rescue is explicitly linked to Abraham in 19:29. No formal covenant event.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Lot is Abraham's kinsman; rescue is explicitly linked to Abraham in 19:29. No formal covenant event.

scenes.title: Abraham and Abimelech
scenes.personsExplicitOrCollective: Abraham, Sarah, Abimelech, God; Abimelech's servants/household collectively
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Genesis 20:1–18 names Gerar and narrates Abraham/Sarah/Abimelech, the dream warning, Abimelech's rebuke and restitution, and healing through Abraham's prayer. The text gives Gerar but not its precise modern identification; retain debated regional status.

geography.claim: Gerar named; modern location debated. Do not place a precise point in the Negev without source-specific support.
sources: Sarah is Abraham's wife; no conception/covenant here. Abraham prays for Abimelech's household; keep this distinct from Isaac's birth.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Sarah is Abraham's wife; no conception/covenant here. Abraham prays for Abimelech's household; keep this distinct from Isaac's birth.

scenes.title: The birth of Isaac
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Genesis 21:1–7 records Isaac's birth and circumcision at eight days, fulfilling the promise. Beersheba is not mentioned in this passage: that city appears later (21:14, 31–33), so current scene city label is not supported by the cited verses.

geography.claim: Birth location UNKNOWN in 21:1–7; Beersheba city-context label is anachronistic if attached to this scene alone.
sources: Direct fulfillment of Isaac promise and named Abraham/Sarah parentage; preserve Isaac as covenant line (Gen 17:19–21), while Ishmael remains separately named.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Direct fulfillment of Isaac promise and named Abraham/Sarah parentage; preserve Isaac as covenant line (Gen 17:19–21), while Ishmael remains separately named.

scenes.title: A well at Beersheba
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Genesis 21:22–34 names Abimelech, Phicol, Abraham, oath, and well at Beersheba; Abraham plants a tamarisk and invokes the LORD. The scene's title 'A well at Beersheba' is text-supported, though not one excavated well identified by these verses.

geography.claim: Beersheba named; well's precise archaeological identity UNKNOWN. The episode follows Isaac's birth but is separated by the Hagar/Ishmael expulsion narrative (21:8–21).
sources: Oath and well dispute; not the Abrahamic covenant enactment. Abraham's household/genealogy context includes Isaac and Ishmael, but neither is an actor in selected verses.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Oath and well dispute; not the Abrahamic covenant enactment. Abraham's household/genealogy context includes Isaac and Ishmael, but neither is an actor in selected verses.

scenes.title: The sacrifice of Isaac
scenes.personsExplicitOrCollective: God; Abraham; Isaac; two servants; angel of the LORD; ram
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Genesis 22:1–19 identifies the land of Moriah, but not a city or mountain peak. Abraham, Isaac, servants, and the angel of the LORD are textual actors; the ram is supplied, and Isaac lives. Jerusalem/Temple Mount association is later tradition, not explicit scene coordinate.

geography.claim: Land of Moriah exact in text; precise mountain unresolved. Jerusalem/Temple Mount is traditional identification and must be labeled as such.
sources: Isaac is named covenant heir (Gen 17:19–21); the oath reiterates blessing/descendants (22:15–18). Avoid identifying this as a human sacrifice completed: text explicitly says the angel stops Abraham and a ram is offered.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Isaac is named covenant heir (Gen 17:19–21); the oath reiterates blessing/descendants (22:15–18). Avoid identifying this as a human sacrifice completed: text explicitly says the angel stops Abraham and a ram is offered.

scenes.title: The burial at Machpelah
scenes.personsExplicitOrCollective: Sarah, Abraham, Ephron, sons of Heth collectively
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Genesis 23:1–20 tells Sarah's death and Abraham's purchase of the field/cave of Machpelah from Ephron near Mamre, explicitly as a burial holding. This is a transaction/burial narrative, distinct from later patriarch burials.

geography.claim: Machpelah near Mamre/Hebron is textual region; traditional tomb precinct at Hebron is not proof of the precise cave/field boundary.
sources: Sarah and Abraham are named spouses; burial purchase becomes family burial context. No covenant enactment, though land possession theme is consequential.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Sarah and Abraham are named spouses; burial purchase becomes family burial context. No covenant enactment, though land possession theme is consequential.

openQuestions: Gen 21:1–7 does not name Beersheba; registry location must remain unlocated absent additional textual evidence.
Moriah's modern point identification remains traditional and should not be encoded as exact.
Gerar's modern identification and the exact Machpelah cave boundary remain unresolved.
